anomaly_def.Name: Schema and Index Design Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description: Definition: Root cause located at the physical data-model layer, where table structure, partitioning strategy, indexing, integrity constraints, or column data types do not match the access patterns of the running workload, so even well-written statements are forced into inefficient access paths. It is independent of statistics freshness and plan-selection decisions and reflects a static design mismatch. Observable phenomena: execution plans dominated by full-table or full-index scans where selective lookups are expected, repeated lookups against non-covering indexes that require additional row fetches, unbalanced partition pruning, integrity-check overhead during data modifications, oversized index sets slowing down write operations, and query latency that improves substantially only after adding or restructuring an index. Possible contributing factors: missing single-column or composite indexes on frequent predicates, missing covering or filtered indexes, redundant or duplicated indexes inflating maintenance cost, inappropriate primary-key choice causing write hot-spots, missing partitioning on large time-series or multi-tenant tables, inappropriate column data types causing implicit type conversions, and absence of integrity constraints that would let the optimizer prune unreachable branches.

entry.official_definition: The number of seconds the server waits for activity on an interactive connection before closing it.
entry.trigger_condition: An interactive session remains idle longer than interactive_timeout.
entry.workload_impact: The server closes the idle interactive connection.
entry.default_behavior: Defined as a MySQL server system variable.
entry.cause_analysis: This timeout is usually triggered when connection establishment, authentication exchange, or session activity does not progress within the allowed time budget.
entry.solution_guidance: Check connection lifecycle, client responsiveness, authentication latency, idle-session handling, and whether connection pools are holding stale sessions.
